channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] EU prosecutors raid far-right Patriots for Europe offices in Brussels and Strasbourg over alleged misuse of parliament funds
item.description: The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) raided the offices of Patriots for Europe in Strasbourg and Brussels.

item.title: [DW] Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
item.description: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Project Fear’ didn’t work, so why do we keep demonising far-right and left voters?
item.description: My beef with both far-right and far-left populists is that they're false prophets. In Europe, at least, the squeezes on public services, high taxes, debt burdens and crippling costs of living are legacies of the Covid pandemic, wars in Ukraine and Iran and a eurozone crisis that was never fully resolved. These can’t be wished away, and they won’t be cured with caps on immigration, higher taxes on the

item.title: [DW] Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
item.description: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

item.title: [DW] Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
item.description: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

item.title: [DW] Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
item.description: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.

item.title: [DW] UK fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
item.description: The UK is sending military support to Saudi Arabia as Iran-aligned Houthi rebels launch repeated attacks on the kingdom.

item.title: [DW] Portugal housing protests continue after police clear camps
item.description: Demonstrators vow to continue their campaign to call for affordable housing in Portugal after police cleared tent camps and arrested at least 55 people.

item.title: [DW] New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
item.description: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security.

item.title: [Politico Europe] This summer’s heat was Europe’s deadliest on record, scientists say
item.description: The continent saw more than 50,000 deaths across 850 cities, with climate change causing most of them, studies find.

item.title: [Financial Times] OpenAI trims valuation target to $1.25tn after pitching higher price
item.description: AI lab floated $1.4tn price tag earlier this month, according to documents seen by the FT

item.title: [DW] Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Why the EU avoids tackling Big Soccer
item.description: A languishing complaint against FIFA highlights the European Commission’s reluctance to take on sports antitrust cases.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s Arctic oil-and-gas pledge leaves a Norway-sized loophole
item.description: If there is no offtake market in continental Europe, no-ne is going to take the risk. The thing is, EU buyers already buy plenty of gas (and oil) from the Arctic.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Parliament defies frugal capitals by seeking €7bn more for the EU’s popular Erasmus+ student scheme
item.description: The parliament overwhelmingly supported an increased budget and scope for the Erasmus+ programme under the new EU budget on Thursday.

item.title: [DW] Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
item.description: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Drones buzz overhead and enemy wi-fi everywhere: Ukrainian veterans describe how they survived in Russia’s ‘kill zone’ (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,701)
item.description: The kill zone’s constant drone buzz, mined roads and invisible Russian networks are making basic things, such as a phone call, into life-or-death gambles for exhausted Ukrainian troops.

item.title: [EU Observer] A bigger EU border force Frontex is set to be unveiled with emphasis on deportations
item.description: The EU's border force Frontex is getting overhauled next Tuesday by a European Commission determined to give the Warsaw-based agency a larger role in deportations, more resources, and more agility to deploy.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs back three-year methane delay, triple what the EU Commission wanted
item.description: The European Parliament has voted to delay EU methane rules for oil and gas importers by three years, two more than the commission proposed. The vote also extends the delay to European producers and opens the door to reopening the law in 2029.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
item.description: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

item.title: [EU Observer] International Criminal Court wins EU’s top human rights prize in defiance of Trump’s sanctions
item.description: The ICC has received the EU’s Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought. The court's president judge thanked lawmakers for the recognition and said "there is no peace without justice and no security without law".

item.title: [EU Observer] Italian MEP on hunger strike over humanitarian crisis in Russian-occupied Oleshky
item.description: An Italian MEP has gone on hunger strike over the besieged Ukrainian town's lack of access to food, medicine, clean water and basic care. The only route to escape is tapped with mines and rife with attack drones.

item.title: [EU Observer] Brussels is moving to ban street advertising by fossil-fuel firms – the EU officials who live there should take note
item.description: Five Brussels municipalities, home to nearly one-in-three of the city's residents, have now voted to drive fossil-fuel advertising off their streets. In the city where Europe's climate laws are written, the industry's grip on billboards and on lawmakers has to be broken together.

item.title: [EU Observer] Serbia’s election: can a student-led movement of hope overcome Vučić’s hollowed-out political system?
item.description: Sunday’s vote could reshape the country’s political future. But even a breakthrough for the student movement would leave a deeper question: can democratic change take root in institutions that protesters say have been hollowed out?

item.title: [EU Observer] Polish parliament liberalises abortion law – but conservative president likely to veto changes
item.description: The Polish governing coalition voted in parliament to loosen abortion law on Tuesday - but conservative president is expected to block the change.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
item.description: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

item.title: [DW] France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
item.description: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

item.title: [DW] How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
item.description: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
item.description: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

item.title: [DW] What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
item.description: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘If stress in France ends up contaminating the rest of the eurozone, the ECB will have to do something,’ says French economist
item.description: France needs spending cuts, but its politics can’t deliver them. Former Macron adviser and economist Shahin Vallée on the protests, Le Pen and Mélenchon’s debt plans, and the dilemma holding back ECB intervention.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Starlink still restricted for Ukraine despite Trump saying Musk lifted speed limits
item.description: Although some Ukrainian drone pilots have reported a marked improvement, there are still "constant connection interruptions."

item.title: [EU Observer] [EXCLUSIVE] Leaked WhatsApps between ex-EU commissioner Reynders and senior Belgian spy reveal attempts to bury allegations of his possible Russia ties
item.description: The messages, seen by EUobserver and published here in full, now form evidence in a Belgian police investigation into Reynders on money-laundering charges, which paints them in a potentially criminal light.

item.description: In der SPD brodelt es gewaltig an der Basis und in der Fraktion. Ex-Arbeitsminister Hubertus Heil bringt sich als neuer Parteivorsitzender in Stellung und sägt am Stuhl von Lars Klingbeil. item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has the world’s war crimes court in his crosshairs.
